adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts the code maps over the full `createdEvents` array to build reference objects (around the shown `createdEvents.map((result) => { ... meetingId: ... result.createdEvent?.id?.toString() ... })`) without filtering out unsuccessful `createEvent` results. From the diff, `CalendarManager.createEvent` can return an EventResult with `success = false` and `createdEvent` undefined (it catches errors and returns `undefined` creationResult but still returns an EventResult). That means the mapping can produce references where the external event id fields (`meetingId`/`meetingUrl`/etc derived from `result.createdEvent`) are undefined/empty, yet they will still be included in references to be persisted/used later. With the new multi-destinationCalendar loop (`createAllCalendarEvents` now creates many events), this per-destination failure case becomes more likely and would leave bogus calendar references for later reschedule/cancel flows to act on.
